text:
mira: Heads-up — noticed sampling flag disappearing on a subset of delayed SQS messages after retries. App-level spans show no sampling decision when the worker picks them up. Anyone seen this?

dan: yikes. which queue? delayed vs standard?

mira: delayed-claims-processor. messages that sit >5m and get retried often. we rely on `traceparent` + our baggage to carry `sampled=1`. seems missing.

raj: SQS message attributes are flaky across SDKs — some runtimes drop binary attrs or truncate. are we putting a full OTLP header into an attribute?

emily: we currently set `X-Redwood-Trace` as a JSON blob in MessageAttributes. example: `{"trace_id":"...","span_id":"...","sampled":true,"baggage":{...}}`. maybe size or encoding issue.

mira: yes. here's a log from the producer: 
```
producer: sendMessage({ QueueUrl, MessageBody, MessageAttributes: { RW_TRACE: { DataType: 'String', StringValue: JSON.stringify(traceHeader) } } })
```
but worker logs show `RW_TRACE` missing on ~12% of retries.

raj: that matches SDK docs — FIFO vs standard, delay + visibility timeout path sometimes re-inserts messages without retaining attributes depending on how DLQ/consumer flow is implemented. Also CF -> lambda transforms can drop attrs.

emily: can we switch to W3C `traceparent` header in a single string? it's shorter: `00-{trace_id}-{span_id}-01`. But we still need to carry `sampled`/baggage.

dan: traceparent has sampled bit encoded in last octet. baggage can go into `tracestate` or `baggage` header but both get long. SQS attrs limit size ~256KB but some middlewares base64 and blow up.

raj: two options: 1) compact binary header encoded as base62 small string (<=128 bytes) and put it in MessageBody envelope; 2) rely on a side-store: put sampling decision and trace key into Redis and include only an id in the message attr. if message gets requeued we can rehydrate.

mira: side-store feels heavier and requires GC and extra failure modes. but robust for very delayed messages where headers may be lost.

emily: what about using the visibility/receipt path to attach attributes on receipt? e.g. consumer picks up, reads body, then explicitly fetches header from side-store if missing. that makes worker logic tolerant.

dan: agree. worker should be defensive: if `RW_TRACE` absent, try: 1) check body envelope for `rwd_trace_id`; 2) fetch from key-value store `trace:ID` with a TTL of 30d; 3) fall back to starting a new trace but tag as `rwd.trace_missing=true` so telemetry shows problem rate.

mira: provisional implementation sketch (node):
```js
// worker middleware
const header = msg.MessageAttributes?.RW_TRACE?.StringValue;
if (!header && msg.Body) {
  const body = JSON.parse(msg.Body);
  if (body.rwd_trace_id) header = await redis.get(`trace:${body.rwd_trace_id}`);
}
if (!header) {
  // start new trace, add attribute for monitoring
  span.setAttribute('rwd.trace_missing', true);
}
```

raj: small note — avoid blocking reads on message critical path. use async background rehydration where possible and emit interim span that links to rehydrated trace (Span Link in OT) when available.

mira: good point. we can: start a local span for the worker, then if rehydration returns later, create a link from the local span to the original trace id. that preserves visibility without delaying processing.

emily: also need to decide canonical header name and format if we avoid side-store. propose `rwd` header compact format: `r{trace_hex}.{parent_hex}.{s}{b64baggage?}` where `s` is `0` or `1`. aim for <=128 chars.

dan: fine, but make sure we also accept `traceparent` and `traceparent+tracestate` for compat. middleware should parse both and normalize into our internal minimal form.

raj: for delayed messages we should increase retention on the trace exporter mapping so that when rehydration links arrive later, they're still useful. currently our Jaeger/tempo retention for ephemeral traces is 7d. rehydration could be >7d for some DLQ flows. ops question.

mira: ops — is increasing retention feasible? infra-bot, any cost estimate?

infra-bot: @mira increasing tempo/trace retention from 7d to 30d estimated +18% storage on hot tier. can be scoped to only sampled=true traces to reduce cost.

emily: that's reasonable — only keep sampled traces 30d, unsampled (0) can stay 7d. also add a special tag `rwd.rehydration_candidate` on traces we expect to be linked later so retention policy can bump them.

dan: rollout plan: 1) implement defensive worker parsing + background rehydration + span links; 2) adopt compact `rwd` header format producer-side for new messages; 3) write migration job to backfill side-store for inflight producers for 48h window; 4) tweak retention/alerts.

mira: sounds good. can we add a quick unit test for message attr drop? small harness that simulates requeue without attrs.

raj: I'll add tests and a small chaos job that flips attributes off before deliver to worker locally.

emily: PR checklist: parse `traceparent`, `tracestate`, `rwd` header; fallback to body id -> redis; emit telemetry tag when missing; create span links when rehydrated.

mira: @dan can you own the retriever middleware? @raj tests + chaos; @emily header spec + export retention change; I'll do deploy and rollout docs.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy triggered for `eng-platform/trace-headers-rehydration` — 1 instance.

mira: thanks all. will follow up with spec doc and short console dashboard to surface `rwd.trace_missing` rate per-queue. :raised_hands:

dan: 👍

raj: 👍

emily: 👍
